lyrics:
[Intro: melodic disco bass line alone, handclaps, a cowbell]

[Verse 1: cool, low, bass and drums]
Took a class, took a trip
Took your photo off the fridge
Learned to cook for only one
Turns out I'm good, turns out it's fun

[Pre-Chorus: strings rise, kick drops out]
So if you're scrolling
If you're thinking of a text
Let me save you the regret

[Chorus: four-on-the-floor, strings, gang answers]
New number, who's this?
Don't know you, don't miss
The way you used to keep me small
Walk on, don't call
If you see me out, I'm dancing
If you see me, keep on passing
New number, who's this?

[Verse 2: cool, a little amused]
Heard you asked about my name
Heard you're sorry, heard you changed
That's so great, that's so sweet
Tell it to somebody else's feet

[Pre-Chorus: strings rise, kick drops out]
So if you're outside
If you're idling in the car
Stay exactly where you are

[Chorus: four-on-the-floor, strings, gang answers]
New number, who's this?
Don't know you, don't miss
The way you used to keep me small
Walk on, don't call
If you see me out, I'm dancing
If you see me, keep on passing
New number, who's this?

[Bridge: bass and claps only, half whispered]
Up, up
Out, out
Over, over
Done

[Final Chorus: everything, cowbell, string runs, ad-libs]
New number, who's this?
Don't know you, don't miss
The way you used to keep me small
Walk on, don't call
If you see me out, I'm dancing
If you see me, keep on passing
New number, who's this?

[Outro: bass line alone, a phone buzzing, ignored]
Who's this?
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 124 BPM, 4/4, B minor. A strutting, four-on-the-floor disco groove. Cool, sharp and unbothered.

VOICE: Female alto, low and cool with a little smoke in it, sung almost without vibrato and with a British crispness on the consonants. Verses understated. The chorus is doubled and punchy, with a group answering on the short lines. Half whispered in the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: An electric bass guitar playing a busy, melodic disco line, the lead instrument. A four-on-the-floor kick with open hi-hats. Handclaps. A cowbell. A string section playing rising runs and stabs. Clean rhythm guitar chops. A bright piano in the chorus. Synth pads.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, the bass line alone with claps and cowbell. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:26 Pre-chorus, the kick drops out. 0:38 Chorus 1. 1:02 Verse 2. 1:18 Pre-chorus. 1:30 Chorus 2. 1:54 Bridge, bass and claps, half whispered. 2:10 Final chorus with string runs and ad-libs. 2:42 Outro, the bass alone, a phone buzzing on a table, one spoken line at 3:00.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Late-2010s nu-disco: tight, glossy and punchy, bass and kick locked at the centre, strings wide, vocal dry and close.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The bass line alone in the first four seconds.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The proof of recovery is ordinary: a class, a trip, cooking for one and liking it. It is a break-up song for someone who has rebuilt an actual life.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Composure, amusement, dismissal, a dance.
